subject: Partner demo runbook + AWS Marketplace bundling and billing flow
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: marketplace-partner@acmeai.com, Jordan Hall <jordan.hall@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: AWS bundling + demo runbook questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the intro. We're finalizing the internal checklist for the joint demo and the AWS Marketplace bundle (ISV SaaS + co-sell). A few quick asks so we can sign off on the integration sprint: 

- Can you share a short runbook that outlines how Redwood expects the demo environment to be deployed (k8s vs EC2, expected infra, sample config)?
- For the Marketplace SKU: how does Redwood want us to present billing (metered tokens vs seat-based)? Any constraints from your side for billing reconciliation?
- Is there a recommended artifact for proofs (logs/KV evidence) we should include in the listing entry?

If easier, we can take a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through. Attaching our proposed delivery timeline.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Director, Strategic Partnerships
ACME AI Solutions

Attachment: acme-project-timeline.pdf (pdf)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Hall <jordan.hall@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS bundling + demo runbook questions

Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks. High level answers below; I attached a short draft runbook and a billing mapping spreadsheet for you to review. Happy to jump on a call.

1) Demo infra: we recommend using an EKS cluster (small node pool, GPU-backed for model inferencing) for the demo. For a lightweight proof we can also provide a single g4dn EC2 instance image. The attached demo-deployment.yaml contains both flavors and an example of the Redwood service config (env vars, model pin).

2) Marketplace SKU & billing: Redwood prefers metered billing tied to token consumption for the bundle, with an optional flat monthly minimum for pilot customers. Metered tokens map cleanly to our usage metrics and simplifies reconciliation. In the workbook I sketched a mapping (metered_tokens -> Redwood usage report export). We can do seat-based only if ACME insists, but that adds a reconciliation delta.

3) Evidence artifacts: listing typically wants an architecture diagram, sample audit log excerpt, and a short telemetry/latency snapshot. We can provide a sanitized export from our console and the runbook describes the path to generate it.

Proposed next step: 30 min call tomorrow 11am PT to align on runbook and SKUs. If that works, Vivek will join for pricing guardrails and Olga will handle technical evidence.

Best,
Rafael
Head of Partner GTM (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: acme-demo-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf); billing-mapping-draft.xlsx (xlsx); demo-deployment.yaml (yaml)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS bundling + demo runbook questions

Adding a few guardrails from pricing & co-sell perspective: 

- Pilot pricing: recommend a capped monthly token allowance (e.g., 10M tokens) with overage priced at our standard metered rate. This makes pilots predictable for procurement.
- Marketplace commitments: if ACME wants co-sell uplift in the contract, we'll want a 6-12 month commit to qualify for certain co-sell incentives.
- Procurement docs: legal will need the SKU description and an example invoice flow; Rafael, please circulate the billing mapping sheet to their procurement team.

Happy to discuss during the call.

--V
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Hall <jordan.hall@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS bundling + demo runbook questions

Thanks Rafael and Vivek — 11am PT tomorrow works for us. A couple of clarifications before the call so we can prep: 

- Can you confirm the level of PKI/KMS integration required for the private data path? Our security team will want the KMS flow documented.
- For the telemetry export: can Redwood supply a sample sanitized log with PII redacted?

We'll bring procurement and a solutions engineer (Jordan) to the call. Looking forward to the runbook review.

Sarah

On Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks. High level answers below; I attached a short draft runbook and a billing mapping spreadsheet for you to review....
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeai.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS bundling + demo runbook questions

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of the call: 

- KMS/KMS rotation: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and can surface a simplified envelope encryption flow for hosted demos. For the marketplace listing, we recommend documenting both options and highlighting the customer-managed KMS as "enterprise" configuration.
- Telemetry sample: I prepared a sanitized latency/usage export (fields removed: user_id, session_id, ip). I'll upload a CSV to the shared Drive after the call and link it in the listing evidence.
- Demo artifacts: Rafael's runbook includes a smoke test checklist; I'll add an extra step for audit log extraction and the command sequence to generate the sample export.

See you on the 11am PT sync.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
